reviews.text: My cat, Jean-Claude, had a digestive problem, so I brought him to Ark for the first time. I was pleased that he was seen pretty quickly. Dr. Rios performed a thorough examination and assessed him to be otherwise healthy—good heart and abdominal sounds. A blood sample was drawn and he was given a shot to help suppress his vomiting and a B-12 injection. We’re waiting to see the results of his blood work, and we may have to get x-rays if he doesn’t rally. Overall, I’m pleased with our experience at this animal hospital. And we’re hoping JC has a speedy recovery.

I’ve been bringing my 6 cats here for the past year bc they’re affordable, nearby, friendly, and in the list of recommended vets from my nearest shelter. Got 5/6 of my cats fixed here. They helped with my cat’s wound infection and ringworm. They’re ever expanding the front reception area to accommodate more customers. They accept walk-ins when appointments are booked.

So here’s why I’m only rating it three stars. The clinic is SMALL. First, the parking is incredibly limited with a fence that limits it even more. I have half a mind to knock it down after bumping my (compact!!!!) car on it. The reception area is UNCOMFORTABLE. It echoes all the loud transit from outside which scares my poor cats and the benches are too narrow and too hard it’s uncomfortable sitting there over an hour. It needs more comfort especially since sometimes walk-ins can take up to 5 hours of wait time because appointments are booked for the next month, and it’s such agony it’s made me seriously consider looking for other clinics.  I recommend either booking an appointment a year in advance or calling to see how many vet techs are actively there the day you wish to walk in. Or be the first to walk in at 8:30am, and I say 8:30 bc sometimes they don’t open at 8am on the dot. From what I’ve seen, lots of dogs come to the clinic, with the occasional cat in their carrier so keep that in mind if your cats are anxious. There is a consultation fee of $40 (plus an extra percent if you pay by card) you must pay up front before they take your pet to the back room, and any added fees like prescriptions and lab work are calculated after. Oh and if you have a voucher for spays/neuters they only accept the discount coupon not the free spay/neuter certificate.

As for the services themselves: they’re fine. Reception is nice. Vaccines are done quickly. They call you once your pet has woken up post-spay/neuter. The vets are kind, bilingual, and clear with diagnostics.

Dr. Saleh is the only compassionate, no frills Vet here. Sad he's only available once a week or so. Staff is ok, though they try their best and could do better, they are ruled by a "Manager", who won't bother addressing patients concerns immediately and will make you wait until she decides you've had enough of a wait. Silly honestly.  Customer Service should be a priority as we are the voices for our beloved pets. But that's what happens when you hire unqualified management. Sinking the ArK. Sad. As for their prices, they're getting up there just as if you would pay at a VCA or PetSmart these days. Same happened at Washington Dog & Cat Hospital.

Unfortunately, since the new owner took over, everything changed in the worst ways possible.
I took my cat here when she started losing mobility on March 10th. I requested bloodwork and a urinalysis, hoping they could use that to figure out what was wrong. They did the bloodwork but tried to send me home with a cup to collect a urine sample because they couldn't due to dehydration. I asked them to give her sub q hydration and try again because I would not be able to get it in the next few days and it was urgent.  They charged me for everything and LIED to me, telling me that they'd gotten what they need and I should receive results in a day or two. I called every day and they kept saying "we can't tell you yet because we haven't received both results". By Friday, March 14th, I was frustrated and asked what was going on. The "Dr." finally spoke to me on the phone and told me they needed to do another urinalysis and a glucose panel. I took my cat in again and asked about the urinalysis and someone let it slip that they never got the first sample, even though they said they did. I also told them to tell the "Dr." that my cat had lumps near her jaw and hind leg, as I was really concerned and her condition was worsening.  The "Dr." never once met with me, only called and when I asked her about the lumps, she said something to the effect of "I didn't notice anything so it must not be a big deal." SERIOUSLY!?!? She sent my cat home with antibiotics...even though what I took her in for was loss of mobility and lumps. My cat passed away soon after. Not once did she ever give me a single productive treatment option or a proper diagnosis. My baby passed away and I got no answers, but they sure did charge for everything they could!

When my other elderly cat started showing signs of illness, I took her in for bloodwork and I was able to see Dr. Saleh. As usual, he was kind and gave me a plan of action. When I was speaking to him and the vet techs, I mentioned I was glad I got to see him and not the other "Dr." as I had found her "useless" and was grieving the loss of my cat.  He called me a few days later with suggestions and to request a follow-up test to rule out certain illnesses.  I told him I would try what he suggested and take her back in a couple of weeks. When I took her back in for the follow-up test, I was pulled aside by a receptionist and told that the owner/"Dr." Hernandez refused service to me because she didn't appreciate being called "useless" (I think I was putting it mildly as there are other words that better suit her and her terrible practices!!!). She banned me and will not allow me to see the doctor I've been seeing for years because of HER EGO. PATHETIC!!!
Her and her team lied to me and ignored serious concerns and I lost my furbaby!!!! Then she proceeded to hinder my access to care for my other cat because she could not care less and it shows!
